dedupe_keys.name: ideamaps emergency obstetric care access deprivation modelled datasets ten cities in africa and colombia

description: These modelled data sets map how hard it is for women in ten cities to reach adequate care during an obstetric emergency, down to 100 metre grid cells. The producers are the IDEAMAPS Data Ecosystem project, led from the University of Glasgow with the University of Lagos, the Urban Big Data Centre and community partners, which also shows the results on its online map. Coverage is Lagos, Kano, Abuja, Accra, Nairobi, Kisumu, Beira, Harare, Pasto and Pereira, each deposited separately on Zenodo in 2025 and 2026. Each grid cell is classed as low, medium or high access deprivation for women aged 16 to 49, combining distance, the choice of public and affordable versus private facilities, and whether facilities can handle emergencies; high deprivation means more than 30 minutes by car to a suitable, affordable facility. The files are free CSV downloads with documentation of format and method, under the Creative Commons Attribution Non-Commercial 4.0 licence. Caveats: a modelled classification, not measured travel, a single snapshot, three classes only, and non-commercial reuse only. Simulation uses: identifying neighbourhoods where the loss of a maternity facility or road would leave women without emergency care, and prioritising new facilities. Related records: the Malaria Atlas travel time maps (data-map-travel-time-to-healthcare) and HeiGIT accessibility indicators (data-heigit-accessibility-indicators) give wider accessibility measures.
name: IDEAMAPS Emergency Obstetric Care Access Deprivation modelled datasets (ten cities in Africa and Colombia)

schema_summary: dataset-output.csv classifies every 100 m by 100 m grid cell into 0 low, 1 medium or 2 high access deprivation to emergency obstetric care; dataset-format.md, dataset-interpretability.md (classification method), dataset-metadata.json and example images

sources.note: Accra: CC BY-NC 4.0; published 2026-01-27; creators Pajarito Grajales (University of Glasgow), Sa'adu Da'u, Baruwa and Elias (University of Lagos), Du (Urban Big Data Centre), Elsey; produced in the IDEAMAPS Data Ecosystem project; maps how women aged 16 to 49 can reach, choose and receive obstetric care in an emergency; files dataset-output.csv (10.9 MB) and documentation

Each 100 m grid cell classed 0 low, 1 medium, 2 high access deprivation; high means a trip of more than 30 minutes by car to a suitable affordable facility; community input from Lagos, Kano and Nairobi
Ten city datasets found: Kano, Lagos, Nairobi (2025-07-29), Abuja, Accra, Beira, Kisumu, Pasto, Pereira (spelt Peiera), Harare (January 2026); all CC BY-NC 4.0

temporal_coverage: Published July 2025 (Lagos, Kano, Nairobi) and January 2026 (other cities)
